risk_if_not_implemented: Without System Privileges Isolation, users, services and processes may obtain or retain access beyond authorized need, enabling misuse or escalation. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Privilege Elevation (R-AC-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2).

compensating_control_1.name: Least Functionality
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to provide only essential capabilities by specifically prohibiting or restricting the use of ports, protocols, and/or services.
compensating_control_1.justification: Least Functionality (CFG-03) provides configuration hardening that compensates for the absence of System Privileges Isolation (SEA-13) by eliminating unnecessary services and enforcing secure settings to reduce inherent exposure. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Process Isolation
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to implement a separate execution domain for each executing process.
compensating_control_2.justification: Process Isolation (SEA-09) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of System Privileges Isolation (SEA-13) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Technology applicability. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
